§1
Warm-Up · Module Quick-Fire
One question from each session · Activate everything you learned in M5
8 min
From S1A · Skills
Say ONE thing you can do well and ONE thing you can't do yet. Use: "I can ___, but I can't ___ yet."
From S2A · Likes
Tell your partner TWO things you like at work and ONE thing you don't like. NOUNS only — no gerunds.
From S3A · Requests
Your colleague asks: "Can you help me with the report?" — Answer with the colloquial phrase. Then ask them something using "Can I…?"
From S4A · Needs
Look around. Name 3 things you need right now — for your work or your desk. Use: "I need a ___ / I need ___."
Run this as a FAST round — 2 minutes maximum. No corrections yet. Goal: activate all M5 content before assessment. Say: "We did this module together. Today is your exit day — you show me what you can do. Start with the person next to you." After the 4 questions, say: "Good. Now you're warm. Let's review everything before the exit task." This framing reduces anxiety and increases buy-in.
8 minutes · 4 questions · 2 min each · Badge b1 on completion
§2
Speaking · Integrated Review
3 rounds combining all M5 grammar · Opinion Meter · Role-play warm-up
10 min
"You need English to have a good career in México today."
Disagree50/50Agree
50%
T–S
Your manager from the US office calls: "Can you speak English? What can you do in English right now?"
Answer in 4 sentences: 2 things you can do, 1 thing you can't yet, 1 thing you like about English class.

"Yes, I can speak English — a little! I can write emails and I can understand meetings in English. I can't speak very fast yet, but I'm working on it. I like English class — it helps my job."

Check all three structures present: can · like · (implicit need)

S–S
Partner role-play — cafeteria at Lumina Finance. Partner A is the customer, Partner B works at the counter. Complete a full order using: I'd like… / Can I get a…? / Anything else? / That's all, thanks. Then switch roles.

A: "Can I get a coffee and a sandwich, please?"
B: "Sure, no problem! Anything else?"
A: "I'd like a water too. That's all, thanks."
B: "Here you go! Have a great day."

Target: natural, confident, no pause to think about the phrases

Class
Class survey: "What does your IDEAL workday look like?" Each student gives ONE sentence for each: what they can do, what they like, and what they need in their perfect work day.

"In my ideal workday, I can work from home, I like short meetings and I like a good lunch, and I need a fast computer and good coffee!"

Note: This is the integrated production target. All three structures in one paragraph = exit-ready.

Round 3 (Class Survey) is the most diagnostic. Listen for: (1) "I like working" → correct to "I like work / I like my job" — gerund still blocked at A1.1. (2) "I can to manage" → correct immediately. (3) 3rd person errors: "She need" → "She needs". Students who can do all three structures in Round 3 without prompting are ready for the exit task. Students who struggle → pair them with a stronger student in §7.

§4
Colloquial Review · Vote Your Favorite
All 4 phrases from M5 · Which one did you use this week?
6 min

Click the phrase you used — or want to use — most this week. You can only vote once.

"Sure, no problem!"
Responding to any "Can you...?" request. Sounds natural and professional. Replaces stiff "Yes, I can."
Click to vote
"I'm not really into [X]."
Saying you don't like something — politely, naturally. Works in cafeteria, meetings, social situations.
Click to vote
"Can I get a...?"
American English informal ordering. More natural than "I want..." in most workplaces.
Click to vote
"That's all, thanks."
The perfect closing for any order or request. Clean, professional, natural. Use it every day.
Click to vote
After voting, run a 90-second role-play: Teacher gives a situation, student responds with the correct phrase. "I ask you for help with a report — what do you say?" → "Sure, no problem!" "You don't like spicy food — how do you say it politely?" → "I'm not really into spicy food." The goal: zero thinking time. These phrases should be automatic before the exit task.
§5
Grammar Review · Error Correction + Reorder
Complete grammar summary · Find the errors · Reorder to correct
12 min
StructureAffirmative ✓Negative ✗Question ?
can / can't I can speak English.Subject + can + base verb (NO "to") She can't fix it.Subject + can't + base verb Can you drive?Can + subject + base verb?
like + noun I like coffee.Subject + like/likes + noun (NO gerund) He doesn't like rice.don't/doesn't + like + noun Do you like salad?Do/Does + subject + like + noun?
need/want + noun I need a charger.Subject + need/want + noun I don't want tea.don't/doesn't + want/need + noun Does she need a pen?Do/Does + subject + need/want + noun?
I'd like… (chunk) "I'd like a coffee and a sandwich, please."Fixed phrase for ordering — always I'd like + noun. Contracted: I would like → I'd like.
Before the activities, elicit the table from students — DON'T show it first. Say: "I know you know this. Tell me: what do I put after 'can'?" (base verb). "After 'like'?" (noun, NO gerund). "3rd person 'need' — she...?" (needs). Build the table together, THEN confirm with the reference. Students who can build it without looking are exit-ready.
✏️ Activity A — Fix the Error
1. "He can to speak three languages."
2. "I like drinking coffee in the morning." — Is this correct at A1.1?
3. "She need a new notebook for the meeting."
4. "Can I have a coffee, please?" — Is this a correct request?
✏️ Activity B — Module Rules: True or False?
"I like working" is correct at A1.1 — the gerund is fine after 'like'.
"Can you help me?" is a correct and natural way to make a request.
"She don't like rice" is the correct negative form with 3rd person.
"I'd like a sandwich" uses 'I would like' — it is a fixed chunk for ordering.
§6
Listening · A Day at Lumina Finance
~170 words · All M5 structures · Monologue · 4 comprehension questions
10 min
"My Day at Lumina Finance" — Lumina Finance, Querétaro
A1.1 · M5 · S5 · Voice: Grace (Customer Service) · Speed: 0.78
0:00 / --:--

Hi, my name is Sofia Reyes. I work at Lumina Finance in Querétaro, and today I want to tell you about my typical workday.

In the morning, I can do many things. I can write reports in English and Spanish, and I can manage the schedule for my team. I can't design graphics — that's my colleague Marco's job. But that's okay! We work together and help each other.

At lunchtime, I go to the cafeteria on the second floor. I like salad and fruit — I eat the same thing almost every day. I'm not really into fast food. I'd like a coffee too, of course! Can I get a black coffee, please? That's all, thanks.

For my afternoon work, I need my laptop, a notebook, and a good charger — my battery doesn't last very long! I also want a quiet space. I don't like loud offices. I need to concentrate.

My team is great. My colleague Ana can speak four languages — I can't do that! But I can help with Excel, and she needs that. So we work well together. That's my day at Lumina Finance. Can you do all these things in English now? I think you can!

📎 ElevenLabs · Voice: Grace (Customer Service) · Speed: 0.78 · A1.1 M5 S5 · approx. 190 words / ~70 sec · Monologue
1. What CAN'T Sofia do at work?
2. What does Sofia like for lunch?
3. True or False: "Sofia needs a charger because her battery doesn't last long."
4. True or False: "Sofia's colleague Ana can speak two languages."
First listen: No questions. Students just listen. After: "What did you understand?" — free recall in English or Spanish. Second listen: Students answer the 4 comprehension questions. Third (optional): Pause at each use of can/like/need and ask students to write it down. This turns the listening into a grammar hunt — very effective before the exit task. Sofia's monologue uses EVERY M5 structure at least twice.
§7
Exit Task · Cafeteria Role-Play + Skills Pitch
4-minute performance · No notes · Rubric clickeable · Badge b5 on completion
20 min
📋 Exit Task — Official Scenario
You are a new employee at Lumina Finance in Querétaro. Your manager, Daniel, wants to know what you can do. Your colleague invites you to the cafeteria for lunch. You have 4 minutes to complete this role-play — no notes allowed.
1
Introduce yourself to Daniel (Teacher). Say your name, 3 things you CAN do, and 1 thing you CAN'T do yet. Use: "I can ___, but I can't ___ yet."
2
Tell Daniel what you LIKE about the job. Say 2 things you like and 1 thing you're not really into. Use: "I like ___. I'm not really into ___."
3
Go to the cafeteria with your colleague (Partner). Order at least 2 items. Use: "Can I get a ___?" + "I'd like ___." + "That's all, thanks."
4
Your colleague asks: "What do you need for your desk?" Name 3 things. Use: "I need a ___, a ___, and ___."

During task: Do NOT correct during the performance — only the rubric matters. Passing score: 10/14 = Module Complete. Below 10 = schedule a 15-min review session before M6.
